title: setup_in_progress can claim nothing changed after Ward created the vault directory or removed a stale lock
description:
Found by the independent review of WCLI-27 (opum-ai/ward-cli#51), which falsified the reason WCLI-27's AC2 audit gave for calling setup_in_progress clean. Not fixed there: a third catalog string is new wording, and new wording is the operator's, not a worker's, under DEC-10's scope. Routed through opum-agent to opum-doc. Blocks nothing.

THE EVIDENCE. src/adapters/setup-session.ts:99-103 opens the setup lock with O_CREAT | O_RDWR | O_NOFOLLOW, so the raise at :114 does NOT require a lock file to pre-exist; the site's own comment at :110-111 records that a NON-contention flock failure is reported as setup_in_progress too. Two paths can therefore change something before the raise. (a) On macOS, :189 prepareVaultDirectory creates the vault directory when it is absent, and a non-contention flock failure -- or a create-and-flock race with a concurrent setup -- then reports setup_in_progress after that mkdir landed. (b) Off macOS, the second-attempt raise at :237 follows clearStaleLock, which may rmSync a stale setup.lock at :154, so this run deletes a stale lock and then reports that nothing was changed.

WHAT IS TRUE WHERE. The contention path -- the realistic one, and the only one on the committed platform -- cannot follow a change, because another process holds a lock inside a directory that must already exist. Off macOS the claim is not true by construction. The remaining macOS question is whether creating an empty private vault directory counts as "a successful write" for the purpose of the claim. That is a judgement, not a measurement, and this fleet prefers to remove a judgement rather than document one.

A/B. A: scope the string to what is true in every raise path -- the vault's setup state rather than the run -- the way WCLI-27 made project_file_unwritable and vault_busy true. B: keep the string and record the judgement that the vault directory is a precondition rather than a change, naming the platform the claim holds on and the off-platform path where it does not.

MEASUREMENT LIMIT, STATED SO IT IS NOT SCORED AS COVERAGE. Neither path can be reproduced on this machine: a macOS non-contention flock failure cannot be induced, and the non-darwin fallback is gated on process.platform and is not a committed platform (ADR-0004; the platform queues are WCLI-21 and WCLI-22). Expect either to reason rather than reproduce, or to restructure so the ordering becomes provable -- for instance by not creating the vault directory until after the lock is held.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The decided outcome is implemented and recorded with the accepted decision source: either the setup_in_progress message is scoped to what is true in every raise path and a test pins it, or the task records the reading under which the current string is true and names the platform that reading holds on
The stale-lock path is addressed explicitly: either its rmSync no longer precedes a setup_in_progress raise in the non-darwin fallback, or the record states why that path is out of scope

plan: 2. Change setup_in_progress.message in src/contract/errors.ts to the DEC-13 wording, one line
3. Add a test pinning the exact string, in the contract errors block
4. bun run check; commit, PR, required checks green, merge
5. Record AC1/AC2 evidence incl. that the restructure is out of scope per DEC-13; close in the PR
implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTED PER DEC-13 (accepted A), read from opum-ai/opum-agent at origin/main 7be97e7, .quest/planning.json: the outcome quotes the operator's first-party answer via opum-doc, relay R-2026-09-29-02, recorded 2026-09-29T09:11:10Z. src/contract/errors.ts now carries exactly "Another Ward setup appears to be running on this machine. Ward did not create a key or a vault." A contract test ("setup_in_progress claims only what holds on every raise path", in test/contract.test.ts's errors block) pins that exact string and asserts the old "Nothing was changed" wording is absent. bun run check 626/626. AC1 satisfied: the decided outcome is implemented, the accepted decision source is named above, and the test pins the string. AC2 satisfied by the record rather than the code, which is what DEC-13 requires: its own words are "The restructure (create the vault directory only after the lock is held) is not part of this answer", and the new wording is true on the stale-lock path as well — a removed stale lock is neither a key nor a vault — so the rmSync-before-raise ordering is left unchanged deliberately and the lock ordering was not restructured. The evidence this task was filed on (the review of WCLI-27 that falsified the old claim; the two raise paths at src/adapters/setup-session.ts:114 and :237) is unchanged by this edit and is not re-measured here — neither path reproduces on this machine, as the task record already states.
finalSummary: setup_in_progress's message no longer claims the run changed nothing. Per DEC-13 option A (operator, first-party, relay R-2026-09-29-02, read at opum-ai/opum-agent origin/main 7be97e7), it is now exactly "Another Ward setup appears to be running on this machine. Ward did not create a key or a vault." — true on every raise path, including the two that can follow a real change: prepareVaultDirectory creates the vault directory before the lock on macOS, and the off-macOS fallback's clearStaleLock removes a stale lock before the second-attempt raise. A contract test pins the exact string and the absence of the old wording. The restructure that would make a stronger claim true — creating the vault directory only after the lock is held — is out of scope by the same decision and is recorded rather than built; the lock ordering is untouched. bun run check green, 626/626; required checks green on the change commit a8ac1ef (Check run 36549068289).
